# 1.2.118 - one day's board at both ends of the day with the school's mood, the opening's veil without Foundry's hidden, a thread's ruling card answered from the chat log, a second GM's frame, the Facilities window's words, and an Eclipse move charged room by room

One stage ships: E118 (tools/stages.json), three lines merged into the assembly. E112v: the opening's veil is the
module's own mark, no longer Foundry's **hidden**, with a rule that a token the module hides gives no sight (the fix of
LIVE-E112-01, the open defect 1.2.117 named). F118: the owner's table reports of 16-18.11.2026 - one day's board at both
ends of the day, a thread's ruling card in the GM's chat log, a second GM's token frame and the Facilities window. C1:
the harness's stand-in for Foundry brought to what line L1 read of Foundry 14.370 on the owner's sandbox (what was not
read is assumed, LIVE-E39-02 to -19), and the module fixes that found. **E39, E40, E43, E53, E58 and E83 are not
shipped** and move to 1.2.119 (tools/stages.json, 46c25c09). E26 stays 1.3.0. From e867ba26 (main at 1.2.117, tag
v1.2.117) to 46c25c09: 72 commits, 7 of them merges - 3 of the lines into the assembly and 4 of line L1's work into C1's
(`git rev-list --count` and `--merges --count` over e867ba26..46c25c09); this release commit comes on top.

In plain words. Everything below is read off the code and the headless harness; none of it has run on a real Foundry or
at a table (## Checked).

**One day's board, at the start and at the end of the day** (F118; the owner, 18.11.2026: "od teraz zarowno ekran
poczatku jak i startu sesji niech wyglada tak samo, czyli ekran zywych uczniow + nastroj szkoly", and "I ten ekran ma
byc identyczny zarowno na start jak i na koniec dnia").
- When Night begins (at the Night Eclipse's end, or at **Skip the Eclipse** from Evening), with the table's sequences
  on, everyone sees the day's board titled "End of day N"; when the next day begins, the same board titled "Day N".
  Under the title both show the same things: the chapter, the time of day and how many are alive, the cast with the dead
  greyed, and **the school's mood** (Calm, Uneasy or Close to spilling; players see only the word). In the morning the
  GM's morning line follows the mood (sequence.mjs `dayBoardElement`, `drawDayBoard`).
- The start-of-day board shows the mood for the first time (66a0c9b4). The end-of-day board no longer lists what each
  student did that day, the day's tally or "What the school saw" (55719596).
- What was done in the Evening now comes as its own summary when Night begins, as every other time of day's does; it was
  folded into the end-of-day board (day-summary.mjs `sumUp`; tier 2 F118-T1, red before the change).
- The next morning from the End of chapter screen now has a fresh mood, worked out as a normal morning's is; before, its
  boards showed the word the clock last held (chapter.mjs, the `morning` step).
- A Spectator's end-of-day board still holds only the title and the mood; its start-of-day board is everyone's
  (sequence.mjs `dayEndBoardFor`, `dayBoardOf`; scenario 93 and R3868 read the end board; the start board is read off
  the code). The end-of-day board's card still stays in the notice history. A world whose clock holds no mood shows no
  mood line.
- The GM handbook and the player handbook, English and Polish, describe the one board.

**The opening's veil no longer uses Foundry's hidden** (E112v; the owner's decision of 16.11.2026, road (b)).
- 1.2.117's open defect, measured by line L1 on Foundry 14.370 with token vision on: while the opening waited, Foundry
  gave the killer no sight from their own hidden token, so they saw from the victim's token instead.
- The veil is now the module's mark alone, `flags.danganronpa-rpg.veiled`; the killer's tokens keep whatever **hidden**
  they had (mask-gm.mjs `veilPatch`). Each browser hides them itself, as it hides a token in another room: the victim, a
  bystander and a Spectator do not see them, their nameplate or their ruler; the killer and the GMs do, and a third on
  the killers' side by the room rule (visibility.mjs `tokenShownTo`; R7702, R7703 and scenario 21, on the harness's
  model of Foundry's refresh). So the killer's own token stays their vision source (R7701, on a stand-in of Foundry's
  rule; not yet on a real canvas, LIVE-E112V-01). The microphone is held as before (code unchanged).
- **A token the module hides gives no sight** (visibility.mjs `installSightRule`): the veiled killer's token gives the
  victim and bystanders no sight of the map around it. The same rule reaches past the veil: on a scene with token vision
  on, a player who controls no token with sight no longer sees from characters the module hides from them - those in
  other rooms with the room rule on, and in an Eclipse every character but their own. While the room fog is on, a scene
  with rooms has token vision off (fog.mjs `applySceneVisionMode`), so there the rule changes nothing. Read on the
  predicate and a stand-in token class (R7706, R7707), not on Foundry's own class (Known gaps). The diagnostics'
  contract list has a new row for it, `token-sight`.
- On a GM's screen the killer's tokens no longer look hidden: the veil writes no **hidden**, and a GM's browser draws
  them as Foundry does (read off the code; not seen on a canvas).
- A **hidden** a GM puts on a veiled token is the GM's and is kept: the token is out of the room for the module as any
  token a GM hid (utils.mjs `hiddenByGm`, R7705). Before, the veil's mark let a killer the GM had hidden by hand back
  into the room.
- What a console still reads: every browser that hides the killer's tokens must be told which ones, so the veil's mark
  reaches every browser and a console can still tell whose tokens they are. The known leak `foundry-veiled-token-actor`
  stays, narrowed to the mark: no character token turns hidden for the veil any more (scenario 21). README.md's sentence
  says so (46c25c09).

**A thread's ruling card answered from the chat log** (F118; AUDIT 9.2 S7-2, measured by line L1 on Foundry 14.370).
- A player's statistic proposal that belongs to a messenger thread reached the GM's chat log with **Approve**, **Change
  to** and **Refuse** buttons that did nothing (a real click, 20 s, no error). On a GM they now rule the card, as the
  messenger's do (gm-bridge.mjs `registerGmBridge`).
- A card already answered, in the messenger or by another GM, is not ruled again from the log: a click there is refused
  and leaves its buttons disabled (messenger-app.mjs `wireCallActions`; bridge-asks.mjs `claimCard` still refuses a
  second ruling).
- Both read by two tier-2 tests that click the log's copy in the harness's jsdom; a real click on v14 is LIVE-F118-01.

**A second GM's character has its frame** (F118; the owner, 17.11.2026: "Nowy blad - na tokenie drugiego gma nie ma
ramki").
- A character that some user has as their own (Configure Player, Character) is framed on every screen - on that user's
  as theirs, on everyone else's as the other students are - a second GM's or an Assistant's included. Before, only a
  character a player owned was framed, so a GM's own character stood bare like Monokuma (own-ring.mjs `frameFor`,
  R7790).
- Monokuma stays bare on every screen but that of a GM who has it as their own character (bone there, as before), and so
  does a character nobody has as their own. In the code, a change of anyone's assigned character or role, or a user
  added or removed, redraws the frames on every screen; the redraw on a role change is held by no test (Known gaps).
  R7790 reads the rule on stand-ins and a tier-2 test the frames on one GM's screen in the harness; frames on a canvas
  with two GMs are LIVE-F118-02.

**The Facilities window's words** (F118; the owner, 17-18.11.2026: "Opis nie uwzglednia akcji pokoju gma i projektow.
Szary druk pod poszczegolnymi akcjami, zwlaszcza restow wymaga poprawy.").
- The tile's hint and description name the window's three kinds: a rest in a room the GM marked for it, an action the GM
  gave the room (with a roll), and a completed project's action (no roll), English and Polish (config.mjs
  `ACTIONS.rest`).
- A rest this room does not allow reads "Not here." on its row, with no list of rooms (the owner, 18.11.2026: "Nie
  chcemy tej listy pokojow w opisac restow"). Trying to rest in the wrong room still names where the character can rest,
  now only the rooms they know of and can enter - their own bedroom as "your bedroom", nobody's rooms, and another
  student's only with its key in hand (rest.mjs `restRoomsSentence`, R7791).
- A room action that costs nothing reads "Free." where it read "Costs 0 actions." (action-facilities.mjs `priceLine`,
  R7792).
- The grey line under a row has more contrast: a closed row's reason went from 2.08:1 to 6.79:1 under Stained Glass and
  from 3.02:1 to 4.68:1 under Monokuma Legacy, at least 11 px at 100 % Interface scale. Measured in Chromium on the
  window as the harness drew it (audit/style-harness.html, docs/dev/f118/shots), not at a table (LIVE-F118-03). The rule
  is the choice rows' (`.drpg-choice`), so every window built of them takes it.

**An Eclipse move through several rooms is charged room by room** (C1; line L1's reading on Foundry 14.370,
LIVE-E05-13).
- On 14.370 one move with waypoints is one update, and the module read only its two ends: in an Eclipse with two
  crossings, a move from Dorm A through the Cafeteria and the Hall to the Storage ended in the Storage, a room past the
  allowance, and the Cafeteria never counted.
- Now each room on the route is counted, and a move a room past the allowance stops at its last allowed crossing; in
  Daily Life each room on the route is paid for (movement.mjs `roomsAlong`, `routeLegs`; scenario 70, R7740). Each leg
  of the route is judged on its own, so a lawful route to a room that is not next to the start is no longer refused, and
  a route with an unlawful leg is refused whole.
- L1's reading was a move made through Foundry's API; the fix is checked on the harness's model of 14.370. A mouse drag
  through rooms was not read (LIVE-E39-11).

**Smaller fixes from C1**
- A GM sending a token back now writes every coordinate it names (movement.mjs `putBackWrite`, with `diff: false`). On
  the harness's model, a put-back written while the player's own move was still on its way left the token at a mix of
  the two spots, two runs in three (scenario 76); now three runs of three are right. Not read on v14 (LIVE-E39-12).
- A GM's own write of a value a player's pending write had already left on the sheet - a Find Stash resolved by the GM,
  a switch in the Students window, among others - is no longer undone afterwards by the module's sheet guard writing the
  GMs' old value over it (sheet-audit.mjs `noteOwnDropped`, resource-guard.mjs `noteOwnWrite`, R7744). Found on the
  harness once it skipped such writes as Foundry 14.370 does (a write of a value already held is not sent); not read at
  a table (LIVE-E39-16).
- A Secret Passage or tunnel made from the GM console with no floor named now takes the scene's floor where the scene
  has exactly one (passages-gm.mjs `floorNamed`, R7742, R7743). On 14.370 every scene has a floor, the default one where
  none was drawn (docs/dev/e39/CALIBRATION.md), so such a passage was refused on every v14 scene; a scene with several
  floors still asks for one. Not tried at a table (LIVE-E39-14).

**Running the suite on a real Foundry** (C1 with line L1; `game.drpg.runTests({ tier: 2 })` at a table).
- For the length of one tier-2 test the suite now sets the dice that test names and answers the windows it queues, on a
  real Foundry too, in the GM page's memory alone; each is taken off after the test, and the run ends by checking the
  dice and the windows are real again (the owner's decisions of 17.11.2026; R7564-R7567).
- Tests that open Daggerheart's roll window press its Roll, as a player does; a test still running after 15 minutes
  fails as timed out and stops the run, with the windows open on the GM's page listed (R7561-R7563).
- The tests' stand-in users are real unsaved Users with valid ids, as 14.370 asks; the Reroll tests reroll the message's
  real roll at a table; the restore puts Daggerheart's Fear back; the window-width test measures its own window.
- The dice and the windows were read on the owner's sandbox on line L1's commits; the whole tier 2 at a table is not
  green, and has not run on this release's tree (Known gaps).

## Before installing

- **No migration step** (scripts/migrate.mjs has no change); a veil standing at the update is converted (below). No
  setting is added or removed (`game.settings.register` on 202 lines of scripts/ at both ends). The GMs' stores and the
  player copies keep their definitions (gm-stores.mjs and gm-store.mjs have no change).
- **A veil standing when you update** (a direct murder's opening waiting on 1.2.116 or 1.2.117): at the primary GM's
  next load, each of the killer's tokens gets its own **hidden** back from before the veil and keeps the veil's mark;
  when the opening ends the mark goes (mask-gm.mjs `settleVeilsNow`, tier 2 "E112v - a veil written by 1.2.116 or
  1.2.117 ...", headless; not tried on a world updated mid-opening). Until that load the tokens still carry the old
  veil's **hidden**. A veil row written from now on says it hides by the module (`hides: "module"`).
- **Language**: lang/en.json goes from 6370 to 6369 keys: 6 added (`DRPG.Action.costsNothing`, `DRPG.Rest.notHere`,
  `DRPG.Rest.noOpenRooms`, `DRPG.Rest.yourBedroom`, and the `token-sight` row's two `DRPG.Contract.*` sentences), 7
  removed (the end-of-day board's rows, tally and lines: `DRPG.Sequence.dayEndSub`, `yourDay`, `tableDay`,
  `foundSomething`, `dayTally`, `quietDay`, `publicEvents`), none changed in wording; the Facilities tile's English hint
  and description changed in config.mjs. lang/pl.json goes from 7457 to 7456: every English key and no other but the
  Polish plural forms (.few, .many; 534, same count) and the 553 DRPG.Config.* keys (same count), two of which, the
  Facilities tile's hint and description, changed. Counted on the flattened files, e867ba26 against 46c25c09.
- No icon is added. No console name changed (tools/api-surface.json has no change in the range).
- **Daggerheart**: `verified` stays 2.12.9. **Foundry**: module.json's compatibility has no change (minimum 14.364,
  verified 14.365); the owner's sandbox runs 14.370, which module.json does not name.

## Known gaps

- **Not shipped**: E39, E40, E43, E53, E58 and E83 (tools/stages.json, planned 1.2.119). E26 stays 1.3.0.
- **No local gate has passed**: E118 declares sockets, rolls and scenes, so the gate is required, and no part of it has
  run on this release's tree; the record in the tree, audit/gate/local-gate.json, is 1.2.117's, every part not run for
  want of a server. Nothing in this release has run on a real Foundry or at a table.
- **Tier 2 at a table is not green**: line L1's last whole run of tier 2 on the owner's 14.370 sandbox, at d5907e1b
  (L1's commit, merged into C1's line; before the window answers, the users' `active`, the form answers, the stand-in
  Users and the Reroll tests were fixed), read 1326 passed, 214 failed, 26 skipped of 1566
  (docs/dev/e58/LOCAL-REPORT.md, "the third run"); no whole run since, on any Foundry.
- **Not yet tried at a table**: every LIVE item this release writes or touches is open - LIVE-E112V-01 and -02,
  LIVE-E112-02, LIVE-F118-01 to -04 and LIVE-E39-02 to -19 (## Checked, the last line).
- **The veil's known leak stays**, narrowed: a console can still list the tokens carrying the veil's mark and tell whose
  they are (`foundry-veiled-token-actor`; docs/dev/e112v/DESIGN.md section 3: moving the mark into each player's copy or
  a packet would only move what a console reads).
- **Open for the owner**: every player observes every character by the module's default ownership, which is what lets
  Foundry give a player sight from another's token; it is not changed here (docs/dev/e112v/DESIGN.md section 5).
- **The sight rule is read on a stand-in**: the harness has no Foundry token class, so whether 14.370's class owns the
  vision test where the rule looks, and whether Foundry asks it there, is not measured (LIVE-E112V-01; the diagnostics'
  `token-sight` row says whether it is installed).
- **Not built**: D7 (a region's owner), D8 (a writer's copy of another User) and D9 (`noHook`) of the calibration
  (docs/dev/e39/CALIBRATION.md section 4); a D for a chat message's rolls, proposed (docs/dev/e39/STATUS.md).
- **Read and left**: a GM's write that removes a key a player's pending write already removed is not told to the sheet
  guard, since whether 14.370 sends such a removal is not read (LIVE-E39-17); the same case on an item's protected flags
  is not built (1c3a7b3a). A frame's redraw on a user's change of role is held by no test (a mutant without it survived;
  LIVE-F118-02).
- **Carried, not closed**: a killer behind a "?" keeps their token's actor (`foundry-masked-token-actor`); 72-canary's
  three expected reds (`foundry-hidden-tokens`, `foundry-actor-items`, `S17-64`); 30-security's two
  (`foundry-secret-door-type`, `foundry-masked-token-actor`), 33-bridge-paths' one (`foundry-cub-purse`) and
  76-passages' one (`foundry-passage-tunnel`); and, in scenarios not run on the merged tree, 65-season's two
  (`foundry-passage-crossing`, `foundry-passage-only-room`) and 67-trial-modes' one (`TR30`).
  audit/harness/known-leaks.json holds these 11 rows, as at 1.2.117; only `foundry-veiled-token-actor` changed.
- **Carried from 1.2.117**: a race in the harness's fuzz (lib/fuzz.mjs), whose clean-up can read a flag clear before its
  last write lands (no change to lib/fuzz.mjs in the range).
- **From 1.2.117's list**: the veiled killer's vision (LIVE-E112-01) has its fix built here; it has not been seen at a
  table (LIVE-E112V-01). The rest of 1.2.117's list stands as its notes give it, E40's and E43's open parts and the
  readings left at the sandbox among them.
